title: needs-decision: idd-advisory-convergence-comment.yml's eager --apply exhausts the rerun-once budget mid-review-burst
body:
## Background

Auditing PR #2628 (still open, ~4h stuck as of this writing) found that
its required `idd-advisory-convergence` check is permanently stuck even
though the check's own live verdict already reports `converged: true,
ready: true` for the current HEAD. This is a genuinely new, verified
finding -- distinct from (and not a recurrence of) the same-HEAD-SHA
duplicate-review-request bug fixed by PR #2633 (closes #2622).

**#2622/#2633 status: confirmed fixed, not recurring.** PR #2628's 6
Copilot review requests each correlate with a genuinely distinct, new
commit SHA -- no same-SHA duplicates. A systematic scan of PRs created
`>=2026-09-04` (30 PRs) found exactly 5 duplicate-SHA instances, all
with `submittedAt` **before** the fix's merge (`2026-09-05T08:40:25Z`);
zero afterward. A second, narrower re-scan of PRs updated since the fix
(2 PRs, #2633, #2635) also shows zero duplicates. The "commits keep
triggering new reviews" pattern visible on PR #2628 is legitimate,
by-design per-HEAD convergence: every one of its 7 commits fixed a
genuinely new review finding (from Copilot/Codex/CodeRabbit), so every
commit correctly earned a fresh Copilot review of the new HEAD.
`idd-review-fix.instructions.md`'s within-round batching guidance
(E9/E12) was already followed -- each push bundles that round's fixes
rather than pushing once per fix, so this is not a batching-discipline
gap either.

**What is actually stuck**, and reproducible with the repo's own
read-only diagnostic tool, is a gap in the rerun-once recovery path
that was never exercised until a PR went through this many rapid
review rounds:

```sh
$ node scripts/rerun-advisory-convergence.mjs --pr 2628
```

All 6 `idd-advisory-convergence` check-run instances for PR #2628's
HEAD report:

- `rerunBudgetHeld: true` (each instance's `runAttempt` is already `2`
  -- its one-time `rerun-once` budget is spent)
- `isLiveCoverageRecovery: true` with `reason: "... a live check now
  confirms the current HEAD is covered by a fresh review; the
  historical hold is stale -- safe to rerun (live-coverage recovery,
  #1806)"` -- i.e. the tool's own live check already agrees the hold is
  stale, on **every** instance
- `counts.pass: 0` -- no sibling instance for this HEAD ever completed
  with a passing conclusion

Despite 6/6 instances independently qualifying for the #1806/#2549
live-coverage-recovery signal, `liveCoverageRecoveryPlan` is **empty**
and the tool falls through to the unconditional
`rerunPolicyHoldNotice`, requiring a maintainer to manually decide.

### Root cause (two related, verified mechanisms)

**A. The non-required companion workflow spends the one-time rerun
budget eagerly, often while the same race that caused the staleness is
still active.** `.github/workflows/idd-advisory-convergence-comment.yml`
fires on every `pull_request_review_comment` / IDD-originated
`issue_comment` and unconditionally runs `rerun-advisory-convergence.mjs
--apply` with no debounce or quiet-window check. For PR #2628 this
workflow fired **30 times within about 15 minutes**
(`06:35:52`-`06:49:52Z`, `gh api
repos/kurone-kito/idd-skill/actions/workflows/337061184/runs`),
matching the pace of disposition/resolve comments posted during a
fast, 6-round review-fix cycle. `gh api .../actions/runs/<id>/attempts/2`
on the resulting `run_attempt: 2` runs confirms `triggering_actor:
github-actions[bot]` -- the automated `--apply` call, not a human or a
`workflow_dispatch`. Because `--apply` reruns the *same* check-run
instance (incrementing its `run_attempt`, not creating a new one) and
the underlying instability this repo's own `idd-advisory-convergence.yml`
header already documents (#1381, #2023: several near-simultaneous
review/comment events racing the shared `cancel-in-progress`
concurrency group) is often still active seconds later, the single
allowed rerun attempt has a real chance of hitting the identical race
again -- permanently exhausting that instance's budget mid-burst, well
before the PR's review activity actually settles.

**B. The #2549 live-coverage-recovery exception requires a passing
sibling that this burst pattern can prevent from ever existing.** Per
`docs/idd-helper-scripts.md`'s own documentation, `liveCoverageRecoveryPlan`
only promotes a `rerun-budget-held` + live-covered instance back to
`rerun-eligible` when a sibling instance for the same HEAD/check
already classifies `pass`, as proof the rollup is "otherwise already
resolved." When mechanism A above exhausts every sibling's budget
during the same burst (as happened here -- 6/6 held, 0/6 passing), that
precondition can never be satisfied, even though the live `--assert`
itself -- the actual ground truth the check exists to reflect -- already
says `converged: true, ready: true`. The exception was designed for
"stale instance, corroborated by a passing peer"; it has no path for
"stale instance, live-verified directly, with no peer left to
corroborate it because the same burst that made it stale also consumed
every peer's one rerun."

Neither of these is the trigger-narrowing or concurrency-group-narrowing
idea already investigated and explicitly rejected in
`idd-advisory-convergence.yml`'s own header comment (#1381, #2023) --
that analysis is about which events *should* trigger the required job,
not about when the *non-required* companion workflow spends the
required job's limited recovery budget, or how the live-coverage
exception corroborates staleness.

## Proposed change

Have a maintainer choose one (or more) of the following mitigations for
the rerun-once budget being exhaustible mid-burst with no automatic
recovery left, even when the check's own live assert already confirms
convergence:

### Options for a maintainer to choose among

- **Option A: Debounce the companion workflow's `--apply` call.** Wait
  for a short quiet window (no new qualifying comment/review/push
  activity for N seconds) before invoking
  `rerun-advisory-convergence.mjs --apply`, so the one allowed rerun
  attempt is more likely to land after the causal race has settled.
  Trade-off: GitHub Actions has no native debounce primitive for
  event-triggered workflows; this needs a bounded sleep-and-recheck
  loop (added latency for the common, non-racy case) or a scheduled
  poll instead of instant event response.
- **Option B: Widen the #2549 live-coverage-recovery exception.** When
  *every* same-HEAD instance is simultaneously `rerunBudgetHeld` and
  `isLiveCoverageRecovery: true` (i.e. there is no non-covered instance
  left, and nothing to corroborate against because nothing ever
  passed), grant one bounded extra rerun on the most recent instance
  anyway -- treating the live `--assert` result itself as sufficient
  evidence, the same class of decision #1997 already made for
  corroborated cancelled/timed-out siblings. Trade-off: loosens a
  deliberately conservative, security-relevant gate
  (`idd-advisory-convergence.yml`'s entire purpose is being robust
  against a weak/careless execution model); needs the same care #1997
  and #2549 themselves already document.
- **Option C: Coalesce/rate-limit the companion workflow per PR.** Skip
  `--apply` if the same check-run instance was already reran within the
  last N minutes, since re-spending an already-failed instance's one
  shot again this soon provides no additional benefit. Trade-off: needs
  a place to persist "last apply attempt time" per instance (no
  existing state store for this workflow today).
- **Option D: Something else / defer.** The maintainer may judge the
  existing `ciGate.externalCheckWaivers` backstop (Refs #1465) is the
  intended off-ramp for this case and no code change is warranted.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A maintainer has recorded which option (A/B/C/D) applies, with
      rationale, as a comment or edit on this issue.
- [ ] If A, B, or C is chosen: the change is implemented with test
      coverage mirroring the existing `#1997`/`#2549` exception-path
      tests in `tests/rerun-advisory-convergence.test.mts`, and
      `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` is updated to describe the new
      behavior.
- [ ] If D is chosen: this issue is closed with the rationale recorded,
      and no repository change is made solely on this issue's basis.
- [ ] Either way, the specific PR #2628 scenario (6/6 same-HEAD
      instances simultaneously `rerunBudgetHeld` and
      `isLiveCoverageRecovery: true`, zero passing siblings, live
      assert already `ready: true`) is addressed by the chosen
      disposition -- either automatically recovered next time it
      occurs, or explicitly left to the maintainer-waiver backstop by
      design.

## Candidate files

- `.github/workflows/idd-advisory-convergence-comment.yml` (Option A/C)
- `src/scripts/rerun-advisory-convergence.mts`
  (`liveCoverageRecoveryPlan` construction, Option B/C)
- `tests/rerun-advisory-convergence.test.mts` (existing coverage for
  the #1997/#2549 exception shapes)
- `docs/idd-helper-scripts.md` (documents whichever behavior changes)

---

_Autopilot suitability: 3 / 5 -- higher is more autopilot-suitable;
below the configured floor is human-oriented. The choice among options
is a deliberate trade-off against this repository's security-relevant,
fail-closed required-check design (#1381, #1424, #1745, #1806, #1997,
#2549) that a maintainer should make explicitly, mirroring the decision
pattern already used for comparable rerun/waiver-policy changes in this
area._

_Effort: M -- author-estimated size; a soft autopilot selection
tie-breaker only._
